claims.text: The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response.
The untreated alloy has poor fracture toughness and tends to crack.
Intrinsic brittleness is responsible for the alloy's poor fracture toughness.
Holding the alloy at 700–750 K for around one hour and rapidly quenching it can induce nanoscale ductile precipitates.
The proposed heat treatment can form the precipitates without substantially altering the primary transformation phase responsible for the caloric effect.
The heat treatment will produce a fine and uniformly dispersed secondary phase at grain boundaries and within the microstructure.
The secondary-phase precipitates will be ductile.
The nanoscale precipitates will impede crack initiation and propagation through precipitation-strengthening mechanisms.
Optimizing precipitate volume fraction and distribution will improve toughness without significantly interfering with the caloric phase transformation.
The heat-treated alloy will have greater compressive strength than the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will have greater fracture toughness and less cracking than the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will retain approximately the same caloric-effect magnitude as the untreated alloy.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during magnetic- or pressure-field operation near the caloric transition temperature.
The intervention is expected to improve integrity under quasi-static compressive loading.
The alloy's transition temperature is near room temperature.
An inert treatment atmosphere will prevent oxidation during heat treatment.
Effects at extreme strain rates or in oxidizing environments are outside the stated scope.
